transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-04-11
Start time: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 47 minutes
Attendees: Maya Patel (Redwood AE), Jordan Lee (Redwood SE), Alice Wong (Aurora SRE), Tom Reyes (Aurora VP Eng), Priya Narayanan (Aurora CTO), Luis Garcia (Aurora Platform)

Summary:
Quick sync to follow up on the 2027-04-09 production incident that caused degraded inference latency and partial timeouts for Aurora's patient-summary endpoint. Confirm root cause hypothesis, align mitigations, and agree next steps and runbook updates.

Topics:
- Incident timeline and impact
- Root cause: autoscaler behavior + continuous batching interaction with KV cache eviction
- Short-term mitigations (fallback model routing, throttles)
- Longer-term reliability items (autoscale tuning, circuit breaker, runbook)
- Postmortem ownering and exec summary

Transcript:
[00:00] Maya Patel: ok thanks everyone for joining. we'll keep this tight 30, 40 minutes. Jordan and i will run through what we saw from our side then hand it to you for the customer view.
[00:18] Jordan Lee: hey all. quick note: i pulled the dedicated pool metrics and there's a pretty clear CPU/GPU imbalance during the window. it looks like the continuous batching queue spiked which led to long queue times and then a cascade where the autoscaler tried to add nodes but kube provisioning lagged. also some kv cache churn - i kept seeing "K V cash" in logs, uh kv cache eviction thrashing.
[00:40] Alice Wong: yeah from our side we saw increased 5xxs starting ~02:12 UTC, and the patient-summary route had ~18% timeouts. our downstream db calls were fine, so we suspected the inference layer. we throttled traffic and shifted critical traffic to the lighter model variant which helped.
[01:05] Tom Reyes: can you explain the model routing bit? the automatic fallback that we configured -- did that fail or was it working?
[01:13] Jordan Lee: the fallback did trigger for some requests, but only after the queue had degraded past SLO. there was a short window where requests were queued waiting for KV cache warm-up and memory pressure caused retries. some of the retries overlapped with autoscaler spikes, causing more connections.
[01:32] Priya Narayanan: one of our concerns is data residency and the fact we run Dedicated in our VPC. i want to ensure this isn't an issue with the private network EBS provisioning times or our cloud provider.
[01:45] Jordan Lee: good question. we checked node provisioning latencies — they were within normal ranges for the cloud region, but the bottleneck seems to be the workload pattern: a burst of long-context requests that disabled effective batching and forced many cold KV cache misses. so it's a mix of request shape and runtime behavior, not purely network provisioning.
[02:05] Luis Garcia: we did have a larger-than-normal batch of nightly syncs that coincided with the customer request storm — our ETL kicked off a heavy job at 02:00. not ideal timing.
[02:18] Maya Patel: that aligns with what we saw. another datapoint: our telemetry shows increased GC pauses on the worker process around the same window; may be exacerbating latency under memory pressure.
[02:33] Alice Wong: do you have the exact trace ids? we can correlate with our logs.
[02:36] Jordan Lee: yes, i'll share sanitized traces. note, some of the ids got truncated in the exporter, so there might be small naming inconsistencies in the bundle.
[02:50] Tom Reyes: from a reliability standpoint what's the recommended short-term mitigation we should apply before the full root cause is fixed?
[02:58] Jordan Lee: immediate: enable model-level circuit breaker and reduce max_batch_size for the patient-summary route to reduce queueing. enable prefix KV caching for that route and increase cache TTL. also temp-cap the concurrent requests per worker.
[03:20] Maya Patel: we can push a config change to your Dedicated pool, but we'll need a maintenance window for risk. alternatively, you can flip a per-route override in your console.
[03:32] Alice Wong: prefer route override so we can roll back quickly. can you walk through the exact console steps?
[03:36] Jordan Lee: sure, go to Routes > patient-summary > Performance Overrides. set max_batch_token to 512, set concurrency cap to 8, and enable fallback to model-variant-b. i'll send screenshots.
[03:50] Priya Narayanan: longer term what prevents this from repeating as traffic grows?
[03:56] Jordan Lee: longer term: autoscaler tuning (scale earlier at lower CPU threshold), split heavier models to separate pools to avoid noisy neighbor, and improve KV cache warm start — we have an option to persist a warm cache snapshot across restarts which reduces cold miss penalty.
[04:18] Tom Reyes: is the cache snapshot feature GA?
[04:22] Jordan Lee: it's in beta but proven in other customers; it requires a small disk provision on the instance and we can enable it on Dedicated.
[04:30] Alice Wong: what about monitoring/alerting? our alert only fired when timeouts climbed, we need earlier signals.
[04:35] Maya Patel: add alerts for batch queue length, KV cache miss rate, and worker GC pause duration. we can provide recommended thresholds.
[04:44] Luis Garcia: any security concerns changing cache persistence? we need to ensure encryption at rest and KMS integration works with our key policy.
[04:51] Jordan Lee: yes it's full EBS encryption and integrates with your KMS. we'll validate with your sec team but technically it's supported.
[05:05] Alice Wong: ok next, on postmortem authorship — we'd like Redwood to share a draft with the timeline and telemetry, and we'll add internal customer impact notes.
[05:14] Maya Patel: i'll own the exec summary and timeline and Jordan will own the infra telemetry section. we'll send a draft by Friday.
[05:22] Tom Reyes: can you outline the scope for the postmortem so we know what to expect in the draft?
[05:27] Maya Patel: sure — scope: timeline, root cause hypothesis, contributing factors (ETL job alignment, KV cache cold misses, autoscaler tuning), impact (timeouts %, affected customers), mitigations applied, action items, and long-term reliability roadmap.
[05:45] Priya Narayanan: one ask — include a short note for engineering leadership that quantifies business impact (error budget burn and customer visible incidents).
[05:52] Maya Patel: noted. we'll include error budget numbers and suggested credits/proration.
[06:00] Alice Wong: what about SLA credits — the incident crossed a latency SLO for one hour, do we start the credits process?
[06:07] Maya Patel: we'll review the SLA clause. i'll include a proposal in the executive postmortem and we can route through your procurement as needed.
[06:16] Jordan Lee: quick technical note: we saw intermittent 13: OOMKilled on a couple of pods during the window, probably due to GC + batch size. i recommend an immediate pod memory bump of 10% to stabilize while we tune batching.
[06:32] Luis Garcia: can we do that without a redeploy?
[06:35] Jordan Lee: requires a config update and rolling restart; low risk if done staged.
[06:42] Tom Reyes: we also want the runbook updated. current runbook doesn't cover continuous-batching edge cases.
[06:48] Maya Patel: agreed — we'll propose runbook changes: pre-defined thresholds, how to flip model routing, where to check kv metrics, and who to page.
[06:58] Alice Wong: for paging, who should be on call from Redwood? a single SE contact?
[07:03] Maya Patel: we can provide a rotated on-call list; for critical incidents we'll have a Redwood SE + AE contact. Jordan will be primary for infra and Maya for escalation.
[07:12] Priya Narayanan: one more thing: we noticed some transcribed names in the traces were off. please ensure the trace bundle uses consistent IDs so we can match logs.
[07:20] Jordan Lee: will sanitize and normalize IDs before sharing.
[07:26] Maya Patel: ok to recap real quick — Jordan will share traces and gpu/nvml logs; Alice will share app logs; Maya will draft postmortem and exec summary; Tom will update runbook and confirm rollback thresholds.
[07:40] Tom Reyes: for the longer-term work, can Redwood help with a bench to simulate the traffic pattern? we'd like to test the autoscaler and batching changes.
[07:48] Jordan Lee: yes we can run a controlled load test in a staging Dedicated pool or mimic in your VPC. we'll scope that as a POC and include recommended test scripts.
[07:59] Alice Wong: ok thanks, that helps. we'll expect the artifacts in the next few days.
[08:05] Maya Patel: final: i'll include a small goodwill credit proposal to cover customer impact, detail in postmortem send.
[08:12] Priya Narayanan: appreciate that. any risk of recurrence while we do the fixes?
[08:17] Jordan Lee: low to moderate, if you flip the immediate route overrides and bump pod memory and enable cache snapshot we expect to drop risk to low.
[08:25] Luis Garcia: timeline for those immediate changes?
[08:28] Jordan Lee: we can apply route overrides today if you give us console access or we can send step-by-step. memory bump and cache snapshot enable will need a short maintenance window — recommended tonight 02:00-03:00 UTC.
[08:42] Maya Patel: all right we'll close — thanks everyone.
[08:46] End of meeting.

Notes about transcription: some product names were transcribed inconsistently (KV cache -> K V cash, nvml -> n v m l), minor truncation of trace ids in exporter. speaker labels are accurate but may include filler words.
